newsitem.title: MEXICO: Sidek and Situr ahead in Mexican stock trade.
newsitem.headline: Sidek and Situr ahead in Mexican stock trade.

text.p: Holding company Sidek and its hotel subsidiary Situr chalked up strong gains to head the Mexican stock market percentage leaders' list at midday on Friday. Traders put this down to unconfirmed reports that the pair were to restructure their problematic debts.
"With Sidek, part of it is that it was very cheap," said Christian Checa, a trader at the Inverlat brokerage in New York.
"As for Situr, we knew Posadas was interested in selling hotels, and it now seems that Hyatt is, too, which would bump up assets a little," he added.
Sidek B series and Situr B series were both 12.0 percent up at midday, with 694,000 and 3.511 million shares traded in the respective shares.
Traders also said the two stocks were buttressed by expectations of a forthcoming agreement with bank creditors to restructure corporate debts.
Sidek officials were not immediately available for comment.
The rest of the Mexican bolsa was sluggish, however, despite the Dow Jones reaching new all-time highs in New York.
The IPC index at midday was 21.98 points up, or 0.66 percent, at 3,340.93.
